rows.canonical: fitplan.PlanSplit (multi-device split x host-offload decode pricer)
rows.definition: The pure pricer that ranks one decode step for every (split mode: single/layer/tensor/expert) x (offload mode: cpu/stream) pair across N identical discrete devices, choosing only among modes the serving engine can execute.
rows.distinction: fitplan.Plan prices one device's capacity and throughput per KV candidate and fitplan.Search picks context x KV x slots; PlanSplit alone decides HOW the weights spread across several devices and WHAT runs the spilled weights. It prices speed, unlike EvaluatePlacement, which checks declared residency only.

rows.canonical: fitplan.PlacementPoolHostRAM (host-RAM offload tier of a tiered placement)
rows.definition: The placement tier between the device pool and the NVMe mmap: weight segments that overflow the device live in host RAM and are read at the host bandwidth.
rows.distinction: HostPoolUsableBytes is the CAPACITY figure of the host pool; PlacementPoolHostRAM is the TIER NAME a placement row is assigned to, and fitplan-placement-pool-nvme is the slower unbounded tier below it.

rows.canonical: fitplan.PlacementPoolNVMe (NVMe mmap tier of a tiered placement)
rows.definition: The last, unbounded placement tier: weights that fit neither the device nor host RAM are read from an NVMe mmap of the model file at the NVMe rate.
rows.distinction: fitplan-placement-pool-host-ram is the bounded RAM tier above it; NVMe always has room (the file itself), so it is the only tier with no capacity figure.

rows.canonical: fitplan attnWidth (attention layers x heads x head dim)
rows.definition: The per-position attention width the planner prices attention FLOPs with: KV-bearing attention layers x heads x head dimension.
rows.distinction: fitplan-attn-layers is the LAYER COUNT input; attnWidth is the derived product that scales attention FLOPs with context length.
